title: SSL & HTTPS
summary: Fixing the browser's "Not Secure" warning: why plain HTTP is unsafe, how certificate authorities and the TLS handshake build trust, registering a domain and pointing DNS at your server, then adding HTTPS two ways: Certbot on the server, and AWS Certificate Manager with an Application Load Balancer. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Secure a deployed web app with HTTPS using a server-installed certificate and an AWS-managed one.

steps.title: Read how Let's Encrypt works
steps.detail: Certbot gets free certificates from Let's Encrypt. Its short explainer covers how a certificate authority checks that you control a domain.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain in one sentence what a certificate authority does.

steps.title: Shortlist a domain name
steps.detail: The lesson registers a domain and points DNS A records at your server (it uses Route 53). Domains cost money, so confirm with the instructors which registrar to use before you buy anything.
steps.doneWhen: You have 2–3 available names written down with their yearly price.

steps.title: Read MDN on TLS
steps.detail: TLS is the encryption behind HTTPS. Read MDN's overview of what it protects.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain what a man-in-the-middle could see on plain HTTP.

concepts.meaning: HTTP wrapped in encryption so nobody in between can read or change the traffic.
A trusted organization that vouches a certificate belongs to a domain.
A free tool that gets and renews Let's Encrypt certificates on your server.
A DNS entry that points a domain name at an IPv4 address.
An AWS service in front of your server that can handle HTTPS for it.
